exposure: presence of the nurse in the delivery room
skin-to-skin contact between mother and child
outcome: practice of breastfeeding in the first hour after delivery
cohort: The study included 244 postpartum women hospitalized at the Obstetric Wards and Rooming-in Wards at the Hospital das Clinicas in Recife, Brazil.
finding: The rate of breastfeeding in the first hour of life was 28.7%, and factors associated with this practice included the presence of a nurse in the delivery room, newborn weight equal to or greater than three kilos, skin-to-skin contact, and vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was identified as a main factor associated with breastfeeding in the first hour after delivery.
cross-section timing: within the first hour after delivery
birth_weight: newborn being equal to or greater than three kilos
